title: Identification of Structural Effects from Projected Cumulants across Multiple Environments
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The quotient identification is proved only under the load-bearing all-order restriction that every latent cumulant-shift vector lies in the plane generated by the observed low-order treatment contrasts.
The advertised if-and-only-if frontier is confined to a union whose no-breakout branch is defined by requiring the legal unequal-effect swap that supplies nonidentification.
Uniform upper bounds hold for arbitrary fixed admissible classes, while matching lower bounds and the consistency converse are proved only for one specially constructed compatible experiment.
The proposed Sachs application supplies no evidence that the latent-plane condition holds.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved 13 statements, including finite-breakout population identification, a pairwise-ambiguous/joint-rescue witness, moment-order sharpness, and randomized calibration through singular and rank-changing covariance. The math panel passed, but the field claim collapsed because the identifying plane is a purpose-defined restriction and the matching minimax lower bounds were obtained only on one engineered compatible experiment. A future re-anchored run would need a primitive d-factor shift model that implies the plane geometry, plus class-wide lower bounds and complete theorem-level prior-art positioning.
tldr: In a new calibrated low-rank multi-environment submodel, any finite projected cumulant breakout identifies the structural effect at the population level, even above the inference order cap; within the bounded legal-swap domain, global no-breakout is exactly source-label ambiguous.  A three-environment construction is ambiguous in every pair yet identified jointly.  On bounded first-breakout shells, cumulant-SVD estimation and conservative Anderson--Rubin length have the sharp weak-flag rates, while externally randomized multiplier inversion gives asymptotically exact unconditional coverage throughout the bounded ambient class, including singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance.
gap: The closest higher-moment paper handles two environments and either one changing component or simultaneous-shift nonidentification.  It explicitly leaves open whether environments can identify an effect jointly when pairwise comparisons fail.  Covariance-based multi-environment methods use a different diagonal-shift geometry and cannot resolve the treatment-versus-latent source label in this model.
fill: The project gives an if-and-only-if observed-law frontier, an explicit compatible-bounds construction proving that its no-breakout branch contains interior unequal-effect laws, a sharp \(d+2\) environment threshold, realizable lower-order-indistinguishable models at every cumulant order, and a rate-optimal inference program whose unresolved generated-projector limit theory is stated openly.
